description: Read `POST /v1/eval` as the camelCase summary it returns. The spec points the response at `SummarizeExperimentResponse` (`project_name`, `experiment_name`, `project_url`, `experiment_url`, ...), but observed live 2026-11-18 the 200 body is `{"projectName","experimentName","projectId","experimentId","projectUrl","experimentUrl","scores","metrics"}`, plus `comparisonExperimentName` when `base_experiment_name` is set. `GET /v1/experiment/{id}/summarize` on the same experiment still answers snake_case, so only the eval operation gets the new shape. The official `braintrust` npm client (3.44.0) declares the same `ExperimentSummary` (`projectName`, `experimentName`, `projectId?`, `experimentId?`, `projectUrl?`, `experimentUrl?`, `comparisonExperimentName?`, `scores`, `metrics?`) and builds it in `Experiment.summarize`. The Python client's dev server sends its snake_case summary through `snake_to_camel` (`braintrust/devserver/server.py`, 0.51.0). Members are required when both live calls returned them. The `scores` and `metrics` values keep the spec's `ScoreSummary` and `MetricSummary`, which match the wire.
